tldr: No major moves from Simplii's direct Canadian competitors today, apart from a BMO quantum-computing claim. The news that sets customer expectations comes from fintechs and exchanges: AI-agent checkout, near-round-the-clock trading, and retail access to a marquee IPO. Much of the rest is Latin American card and Black Friday promotions.
themes: Agentic AI in payments and checkout
Retail access to hot IPOs and new ETFs
Digital banks moving upmarket and into charters
Card rewards and Black Friday promotions

highlights.headline: Klarna is now payable when an AI agent checks out for shoppers via Adyen Agentic
highlights.why: Payment choice is being built into AI-agent shopping flows. Simplii should consider how its cards and wallet-linked products would show up when an agent, not a person, completes the purchase.

highlights.headline: Nasdaq has published a 23/5 Trading Information Hub
highlights.why: This signals that near-round-the-clock US equity trading is becoming a real offering. Simplii's investing product team should check how its order handling, market-data and customer messaging would cope with extended hours.

highlights.headline: Anthropic's IPO debuted on Nasdaq and B3 the same day, with the Brazilian BDR at about R$60 and R$460M traded on day one
highlights.why: Retail demand for same-day access to a marquee IPO is strong, and a local exchange wrapper met it. Simplii should look at how quickly it could give self-directed investors access to major US listings.

highlights.headline: N26 launched Aura, its most exclusive premium account, to pursue higher-value customers
highlights.why: A digital-first bank is adding a premium tier above its four existing personal plans. Simplii should consider whether it needs a higher-value proposition or whether it is leaving affluent digital customers to others.
